previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p allogeneic cord transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting five days. He was found to be dehydrated with orthostatic hypotension and acute kidney injury, with creatinine rising from a baseline of 1.8 to 3.0. IV hydration was initiated, and his renal function improved, returning to baseline by discharge. Stool testing was positive for norovirus, and flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsy showed no evidence of graft-versus-host disease. Liver enzymes remained elevated throughout admission, prompting consultation with the liver team and plans for close outpatient monitoring; allopurinol was discontinued, and Bactrim was held due to transaminitis. The patient's gastrointestinal symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on liver function and restart medications as appropriate.

Name:  ___         ___ No:  ___

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS:  Perirectal abscess.

INVASIVE PROCEDURES ON THIS ADMISSION:  Examination under
anesthesia and open drainage of a perirectal abscess.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:  Perianal pain over several days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:  Mr. ___ is a ___
gentleman with a recent 9-day admission to the Oncology
service with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.  He had a flexible
sigmoidoscopy on that admission and he was subsequently
discharged on ___.  He had worsening perianal pain since
discharge and presented to the emergency room with perianal
pain and concern for a perirectal abscess.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:  AML with bone marrow transplant
complicated by GVHD, stage III chronic kidney disease,
hepatic insufficiency due to the hemochromatosis,
aspergillosis of the sinus and nares, sarcoid, hypertension,
reflux, chronic diarrhea hypercholesterolemia due to
peripheral neuropathy, diabetes, left lower lobe pneumonia
and basal cell cancers.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:  Basal cell cancer excision.

MEDICATIONS:  On admission were acyclovir, carvedilol,
citalopram, fluticasone, mycophenolate, nitroglycerin p.r.n.,
oxycodone, pantoprazole, prednisone, ascorbic acid, aspirin,
cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate, cyanocobalamin,
loratadine, procarbazine, Lomotil.

ALLERGIES:  Benadryl, AmBisone, Flomax and tacrolimus.

SOCIAL HISTORY: ___
FAMILY HISTORY:  Noncontributory.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:  On physical exam he was tachycardic
with left-sided perianal fullness and tenderness on digital
rectal exam.

SUMMARY OF HOSPITAL COURSE:  Mr. ___ was diagnosed
with a perirectal abscess who underwent an examination under
anesthesia with a large abscess drainage with cultures.  He
was placed on oral antibiotics after 24 hours of intravenous
antibiotics.  Malecot drain had been placed for irrigation
and he was deemed appropriate for discharge with follow-up in
the acute care surgery clinic and with his oncologist.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:  The same as preoperative medications
plus antibiotics.

DISCHARGE STATUS:  The patient was discharged to home with
visiting nursing for wound and catheter function.
